subject: GDPR DPA & SCC selection - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Guerrero <elena.g@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: GDPR DPA & SCC selection - next steps

Hi Elena —

Great to meet you and the Acme team this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) GDPR/DPA/SCC: You mentioned Acme requires a signed DPA and standard SCCs for EU data transfers. Attached are two items for your review: a short SOC 2 Type II summary and a draft DPA we typically start with. Please confirm whether Acme expects Redwood to sign as a data processor (controller->processor SCCs) or if you have a different preference.

2) SOC 2 / Compliance evidence: I've attached the SOC 2 summary (full report available under NDA). If your legal team needs the Type II report, let me know and we can share the report and auditor contact.

3) Vendor security questionnaire: Happy to run through Acme's vendor security questionnaire — can you share the file and target completion date? We can assign a solutions engineer to fill the questionnaire and return within your stated procurement timeline.

4) Timeline & legal contact: Can you confirm the legal point of contact for DPA review and the target sign date? You mentioned an end-of-July procurement window; if you can share the deadline we'll prioritize accordingly.

Next steps (proposed):
- Rishi (security/infra) to confirm Redwood's processor/controller stance and propose SCC module.
- Redwood to share SOC2 evidence and a drafted DPA.
- Acme to share vendor questionnaire and legal contact.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_type2_summary.pdf, redwood_dpa_draft.docx

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Elena Guerrero <elena.g@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GDPR DPA & SCC selection - next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the quick turnaround on materials. A few answers from our side: 

- DPA & SCC: Yes, Acme requires a signed DPA and EU Standard Contractual Clauses. For our hosted vendors we use controller->processor language. Please confirm if Redwood is willing to execute the DPA as processor and adopt the controller->processor SCCs (we typically reference the controller-to-processor module).

- SOC 2: We need the SOC 2 Type II report (latest) for legal review. The summary is helpful but legal will request the full report under NDA.

- Vendor Security Questionnaire: I've attached our VSQ (acme_vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx). Target procurement milestone is to have agreements in place by 2026-07-15. Can you confirm whether your team can return a completed questionnaire and the DPA for signature by that date?

Legal contact for contracting: Anna Lee (anna.lee@acme.com) — please loop her on any DPA redlines.

Let me know if you need anything else.

Best,
Elena
Elena Guerrero
Senior Security Program Manager, Acme Corp
elena.g@acme.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Guerrero <elena.g@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GDPR DPA & SCC selection - next steps

Hi Elena / Marissa —

Thanks for the notes. Quick clarification from a security/legal standpoint so we can align the DPA/SCC correctly: 

- Redwood's typical position: For our Hosted API and Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) we act as a data processor on behalf of our customers; customers are the data controllers. For Private / on-prem deployments, the customer maintains control over the environment and configuration — Redwood's access is constrained and we are effectively acting as a subprocessor only where explicitly granted.

- SCC selection: Given the above, controller->processor language is the appropriate module for Hosted and Dedicated deployments. We'll mark the DPA/SCC draft accordingly but will include language covering Private deployments to reflect access controls and responsibilities.

- SOC 2: We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. The attached SOC 2 summary is a high-level extract; we will request NDAs and then share the full report and auditor contact.

- Questionnaire: We're prepared to complete the VSQ. Proposal: Soojin (SE) will own completion of the technical questions and Neha will handle legal/compliance responses. Expected turnaround: 5 business days from receipt of the questionnaire and confirmation of the procurement deadline (you noted 2026-07-15).

Next steps from Redwood: 
- Share proposed DPA marked for controller->processor SCCs and DPA redline instructions (attached: redwood_proposed_dpa.docx).
- Execute NDA to share SOC 2 Type II report.
- Complete and return the VSQ within 5 business days.

If that works, Marissa and I will loop Anna Lee and procurement to get the process started.

Marissa / Rishi —

This all looks good. Confirming: Acme expects controller->processor SCCs for Hosted and Dedicated, and we'll treat Private/on-prem exceptions on a case-by-case basis. Anna Lee (cc'd) is our legal lead and will accept a redline or a completed DPA — whichever is easiest for Redwood; please send to anna.lee@acme.com.

Procurement notes: we've attached an updated questionnaire with a few additional items (see attached). Target: complete DPA execution by 2026-07-15. If you can start the DocuSign workflow and share the NDA link for SOC 2 access, that would be ideal.

Thanks — looping Anna to coordinate legal review.

Attachments: acme_vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx (updated)

Best,
Elena
